clue.text: Tap-dance footwear stuck under piano? Move around

indicators.note: in a down entry, whatever is stuck under something else is written after it

parts.note: piano in music means play softly
a shoe is an item of footwear
to move things around or shift about

explanation.surface: A dancer finds their tap shoes jammed under a piano and is told to get moving.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's footwear sits under the musical term for quiet, giving SOFT-SHOE, then a word for moving around completes SOFT-SHOE SHUFFLE.
explanation.definitionFit: The soft-shoe shuffle is a relaxed style of tap dancing performed in soft-soled shoes, popular in vaudeville.

clue.text: Two-way live broadcasts from this

indicators.note: going two ways means reading forwards and then backwards

parts.note: to live is to be, to exist
the same word taken the other way

explanation.surface: A two-way live link broadcasting from some studio.
explanation.walkthrough: BE is written one way and then the other; the Beeb is the affectionate British nickname for the BBC.
explanation.definitionFit: The BBC, nicknamed the Beeb, is the corporation that transmits radio and television programmes.

clue.text: Goes to limit ball game

indicators.note: to limit something is to hem it in on all sides, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: to quit is to go, leave; he quits = he goes
a ball is round, like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone sets out to put limits on a ball game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ball game' reads as one phrase, but the ball is the round letter and the game alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Quoits is a traditional throwing game where rings are tossed to land over or near a peg.

clue.text: See 1
Bellow's book — boring thing

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for book
an awl is a tool for boring holes

explanation.surface: A reader dismisses a novel by Saul Bellow as dull.
explanation.walkthrough: Bellow looks like the novelist Saul Bellow, and 'boring' like a verdict on his book; here bellow is a verb and boring means drilling.
explanation.definitionFit: To bawl is to shout or cry out loudly, just as one bellows.

clue.text: I swear I might well use it!

definitions.text: I swear I might well use it!

parts.words: I swear I might well use it!
parts.note: surface reading: someone promising they may well make use of something

parts.words: I swear I might well use it!
parts.note: setter's reading: a person who swears, that is curses

explanation.walkthrough: 'I swear' sounds like a solemn promise, but it means cursing; and 'well' itself happens to be a word of the kind in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A swear word is commonly called by this name because many English obscenities have exactly four letters.

clue.text: Still, that's how it appeared to take in rubbish

indicators.note: taking something in means holding it inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: sic is the Latin tag an editor uses to say a quotation is reproduced exactly as it appeared
tat is cheap, worthless stuff

explanation.surface: Someone insists that a thing still looked, at the time, as if it were swallowing rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: Sic is the bracketed Latin note in quotations meaning 'thus it was written', and tat is British slang for cheap, tawdry goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Static describes something not moving or changing, which is what still means as an adjective.

clue.text: Doctor on cue: NHS paragon of old

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are altered

parts.note: the letters are used exactly as printed

explanation.surface: A doctor who turns up on cue is held up as an NHS paragon from the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' reads as a medic to go with the NHS, Britain's National Health Service, but it is a verb meaning tamper with.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonesuch is an archaic word for a person or thing without equal, an unrivalled model of excellence.

clue.text: Trouble getting a short drink? Take over!

parts.note: ado is fuss or bother
a pint shortened to its abbreviation

explanation.surface: A barman in trouble over short measures is told to let someone else take over.
explanation.walkthrough: A short drink sounds like a spirit or shot, but here it is the pint written in its short form, PT.
explanation.definitionFit: To adopt an idea, cause or child is to take it on as your own, assuming responsibility for it.

clue.text: Put out, objections being overturned

indicators.note: something overturned is flipped, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: ifs and buts are objections

explanation.surface: Someone is annoyed because their objections keep being overruled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out' suggests offended; the definition is the other sense, extinguishing a cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: You stub out a cigarette by pressing its lit end down, which puts it out.

clue.text: Get inside when hot female launches line in fancy attire

indicators.note: whatever launches something comes at its very start

parts.note: in means fashionable, the hot thing
F is the abbreviation for female

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits within it
fancy means elaborate or fanciful, so the letters are dressed up in a new order

parts.note: the letters are used exactly as printed
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A glamorous woman in fashionable dress sweeps into a party to sneak inside.
explanation.walkthrough: L goes into a rearrangement of ATTIRE (I-L-TRATE), F starts that, and IN, meaning hot or trendy, comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: To infiltrate is to penetrate an organisation or place secretly, gaining entry by stealth.

clue.text: Moon: top-of-the-range feature to be put in position shortly

indicators.note: what is put in something ends up inside it

parts.note: POS is a short form of position
a hob is the cooking surface on top of a kitchen range

explanation.surface: An astronomer's note about a feature of a lunar mountain range to be positioned soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top-of-the-range' pretends to mean best quality; a range is also a kitchen cooker, and its top is the hob.
explanation.definitionFit: Phobos is the larger and inner of the two natural satellites orbiting Mars.

clue.text: Futile project — but benefit to boxer with broken leg?

parts.note: a boon is a blessing or benefit

indicators.note: a broken thing is in pieces that can be reassembled differently

parts.note: a boxer is a breed of dog
the letters are used exactly as printed

explanation.surface: Asks whether a benefit match for an injured boxer is a waste of time.
explanation.walkthrough: The boxer looks like a fighter with an injured leg, but is the dog breed.
explanation.definitionFit: A boondoggle is American slang for pointless, wasteful work or a scheme that achieves nothing useful.

clue.text: Kindness of Mr Goodman: 'Awfully nice being on the right side of Strictly'

indicators.note: in an across entry, one thing on another comes before it

parts.note: Len Goodman was head judge on Strictly Come Dancing

indicators.note: done awfully means done badly, so the letters come out in a mess

parts.note: the letters are used exactly as printed

indicators.note: the right-hand side of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of the show's name

explanation.surface: A tribute to Len Goodman, the Strictly judge praised for being kind to contestants.
explanation.walkthrough: Strictly Come Dancing is the BBC's celebrity ballroom show, where Len Goodman was head judge; 'on the right side of' reads as staying in favour, but just takes the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Leniency is mildness or tolerance in judging, a merciful gentleness that counts as kindness.

clue.text: Drop off vessel that's capsized

indicators.note: a boat that has capsized is upside down, so in a down entry the letters run the other way

parts.note: a pan is a cooking vessel

explanation.surface: Passengers are dropped off from a boat that has turned over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' with 'capsized' suggests a boat, but the vessel is a kitchen one.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop off is to fall asleep briefly, which is what taking a short sleep means.

clue.text: Celebrate on joining innovative writer on radio

indicators.note: joining means attaching side by side, so the pieces follow one another

parts.note: re means on or about, as in a letter heading

indicators.note: what is on radio is heard rather than seen

parts.note: James Joyce, the experimental Irish author of Ulysses

explanation.surface: A radio show celebrates an innovative writer's work.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the writer is heard; RE is written normally. Joyce and the spelling JOICE say the same.
explanation.definitionFit: To rejoice is to feel or show great joy, the same as celebrating.

clue.text: I say a bird should be tailless!

indicators.note: without a tail means the end is lopped off

parts.note: a coot is a black water bird

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims that a bird ought to have no tail.
explanation.walkthrough: The bird also makes this sound, a tempting false path, but the definition is the exclamation 'I say', and the bird is docked.
explanation.definitionFit: Coo is a British exclamation of surprise, used just like the expression of astonishment.

clue.text: Crack about our tank tops being illuminated

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds another

parts.note: a split is a crack

indicators.note: the top of a word in an across clue is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter
the first letter

explanation.surface: Someone spots a crack around the tank tops on display.
explanation.walkthrough: Tank tops look like sleeveless garments, but tops means first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Spotlit means lit by a spotlight, so brightly illuminated.

clue.text: Faith's video log not very funny ultimately

indicators.note: not means without, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: the letters are used exactly as printed
V is the abbreviation for very

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only a last letter is kept

parts.note: the last letter

explanation.surface: Faith's vlog, a video diary, turns out to be not very funny in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: Faith looks like a person's name, making the video log hers; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An ideology is a system of beliefs, a creed held with conviction, as faith can mean.

clue.text: 'Got horizontal' in ferry, in an obvious way

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: to ply is to travel a route regularly, as a ferry does
to have lain is to have got horizontal

explanation.surface: Someone lies down in a ferry quite openly.
explanation.walkthrough: Ferry is a verb, and its synonym PLY holds the past participle of lie.
explanation.definitionFit: Plainly means clearly or evidently, which is how something done in an obvious way is described.

clue.text: Exploit survey that legitimises using a different name?

definitions.text: that legitimises using a different name

parts.note: an exploit is a heroic deed
a poll is a survey of opinion

explanation.surface: A survey is used to justify going by a different name.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a deed poll is the legal document by which a person changes their name.
explanation.definitionFit: Changing your name by deed poll makes the new name official, which legitimises using it.

clue.text: Focus of eleven rap tunes shows intent

indicators.note: the focus of something is at its centre, so the letters lie within the words

parts.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: Eleven rap tunes show a clear purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters span the end of 'eleven', all of 'rap' and the start of 'tunes'.
explanation.definitionFit: Enrapt means absorbed or engrossed, fully intent on something, like rapt.

clue.text: Dish of egged escalope starters stuffed in roll

indicators.note: stuffed in means packed inside something else

parts.note: a roll is a turn

indicators.note: starters are what begin, so only first letters are taken

parts.note: the first letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A menu dish: breaded escalope served as a starter in a bread roll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starters' and 'roll' sound like menu items, but mean first letters and a turn.
explanation.definitionFit: A tureen is a deep lidded serving dish, especially for soup.

clue.text: Lead vocalist starts in cute number

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: twee is British for sweetly cute

indicators.note: starts are beginnings, so only first letters are kept

parts.note: the first letters of both words

explanation.surface: A lead singer begins a sweet song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' looks like a song for the vocalist to sing; it is the definition, a counting number.
explanation.definitionFit: Twelve is a whole number, one more than eleven, so it is an example of a number.

clue.text: Ship set out bearing tin

indicators.note: to set out things is to arrange them, so the letters are laid out anew

parts.note: the letters are used exactly as printed

explanation.surface: A ship sets out to sea carrying a cargo of tin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set out' reads as sailing off, but it asks for the following letters to be arranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigantine is a two-masted sailing vessel, square-rigged on the foremast.

clue.text: Succeeding vote is in bag

indicators.note: whatever is in something sits inside it

parts.note: to net is to bag, catch
a cross marks a vote on a ballot paper

explanation.surface: A winning vote is in the bag, as good as secured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In bag' echoes 'in the bag', meaning certain, but the bag is a net.
explanation.definitionFit: Next means following immediately, which is what succeeding means when things come in order.

clue.text: The Guardian's intending to stream?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a newspaper refers to itself as 'we', so its intention is the contraction of 'we will', apostrophe ignored
second meaning: to flow or gush out, as tears or spring water do

explanation.surface: The Guardian announces plans to stream its content online.
explanation.walkthrough: Crosswords ignore punctuation in answers, so WE'LL, the paper's own editorial 'we will', counts as WELL; the italic title marks the newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: To well is to flow or gush out, as tears or water pour forth, which is to stream.

clue.text: See 6
Maybe the perennial sound of groups of birds

indicators.note: the sound of something is how it is heard spoken

parts.note: birds gather in flocks

explanation.surface: Wonders whether the unending noise of birds in groups counts as perennial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perennial sound' suggests a constant noise, but perennial is a noun here, a plant that comes back each year.
explanation.definitionFit: Phlox is a garden flower, many species of which are perennials, so it is an example of one.

clue.text: Bank restricting newspaper's influence

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so one piece closes around another

parts.note: a levee is an embankment along a river
a rag is a disparaging name for a newspaper

explanation.surface: A bank tries to curb a newspaper's influence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' suggests a financial institution, but it is a riverbank.
explanation.definitionFit: Leverage is the power to affect outcomes or people, a synonym for influence.
